summary: Unbounded Flask request-path labels grew the production relay's application metrics from roughly 29,000 to 71,000 series; expensive multiprocess collection and serialization drove memory pressure against the 256Mi limit, the sole pod was OOM-killed, and users intermittently saw no available backend.
impact: Production was intermittently unavailable during an approximately 87-minute crash loop, and repeated termination created an unquantified risk of losing active memory-backed relay state; no customer data loss was proven.
fix: The operator paused only token.place application-metrics discovery and replaced the affected pod to clear its pod-level multiprocess metric files, restoring service without changing the image or Deployment; the permanent bounded-cardinality fix, verification, and deliberate scrape restoration remain pending, so status is Mitigated rather than Resolved.
lessons: Metric labels must have explicit bounds, cardinality and scrape cost need proactive detection, multiprocess files must be safely cleared across application-container restarts, and a single replica amplified each OOM into possible total backend unavailability.
